title: Claude Code wiped production database via terraform apply — 2.5 years of data gone
summary: Alexey Grigorev (DataTalks.Club) let Claude Code run 'terraform apply' without verifying state file. Agent destroyed entire AWS prod infrastructure + 2M rows of student data. Snapshots also deleted. 24h recovery via AWS Business Support. Post-mortem: 'I over-relied on the AI agent to run Terraform commands.' Will now stop agent from running destructive infra actions, manually review every plan.
relevance: Perfect. Exactly the deploy-gate wedge. HN top comment: 'I do not let any terraform apply occur via automation.' The narrative already exists — teams need enforcement, not guidelines.
pp_angle: Permission Protocol = the enforcement layer that stops this. Terraform destroys would require explicit human approval gate before execute. This incident proves the wedge.

title: Okta: Human-in-the-Loop approval for high-risk AI agent actions (CIBA)
summary: Okta published guidance on AI in IAM: sensitive operations (deleting prod data) should trigger standards-based human approval workflows via CIBA protocol. Authorization server pauses agent execution and pushes approval request to human's device.
relevance: Okta is validating the exact Permission Protocol concept. They're describing the problem; PP is the solution layer for coding agents.
pp_angle: Okta describes the ideal workflow but focuses on identity layer. PP targets the CI/CD + deploy gate where the actual destructive actions happen.
